title: Approvals
description:
Approvals (ADR-0228): the shapes the agent worker, the approval store in the realtime server, the browser's approval card, OUI's surface runtime and a conversation engine exchange. An irreversible action — a `transaction`, or a `write` declared `destructive` — runs only on an approval the person gave, bound to the exact call by a single-use token.

1. The worker stops the turn at the call and stores it (`PendingApprovalInput`); the person's tab receives `agent:approval_required` (`ApprovalRequiredEvent`) and renders the approval card from its `preview`, whose every word comes from the action's declaration, never from the model.
2. In a UI only a click on the card counts: the card sends `approval:decide` (`ApprovalDecidePayload`) from the person's own socket. On a conversation channel, the verbatim `readback` and an affirmative next turn (ADR-0210 §2.6).
3. The store answers the decider only (`ApprovalDecideResult`): a single-use token, a compact JWS (`ApprovalTokenClaims`), and the call's `argsHash`. The tab's OUI runtime holds an `ApprovalGrant`.
4. The next turn carries the token (`ApprovalContinuation`); the worker redeems it for the stored call, exactly (`ApprovedCall`), and runs it. A UI action request then carries `approval` (`ActionRequestApproval`), which the browser checks against its grant before it runs the handler.

The args hash is SHA-256 over the RFC 8785 (JCS) canonical JSON of the call's arguments, lowercase hex; `oui-spec/approval-vectors.json` holds every implementation, in any language, to it.

ArgsHash.description: SHA-256 of the RFC 8785 canonical JSON of a call's arguments, lowercase hex.

ApprovalChannel.description: Where the person confirmed. In a UI only a click on the card counts (`ui`); in a conversation channel, the verbatim readback and an affirmative next turn (ADR-0210 §2.6).

ApprovalPreviewArgument.description: One argument of the call, as the person reads it: its declared label and its value in words.

name.description: The argument's name in the call.

label.description: Its label, from the action's input schema.

ApprovalPreview.description: What the person is asked to approve. Every word comes from the action's declaration (its title, description and input schema labels), never from the model (ADR-0228 §2.2).

consequence.description: What running it does, from the declaration.

readback.description: One sentence composed from the fields above, read or sent verbatim on a conversation channel.

ApprovalEffect.description: The effect the approval is for: the action's declared effect kind (ADR-0226 §2.6, `transaction` for an irreversible external act), or `write` when it declares none.

PendingApprovalInput.description: A call waiting for the person's approval, as the worker stores it (`POST /internal/approvals`).

userId.description: The user whose turn made the call: the only one who may decide it.

argsSensitive.description: Whether the arguments may be written to logs. They are only when the declaration says they are not sensitive.

expiresAt.description: Epoch ms, at most 30 minutes away (`MAX_APPROVAL_TTL_MS`).

ApprovalRequiredEvent.description: `agent:approval_required`: the worker stopped the turn at a call that needs the person's approval. The approval card renders it.

ApprovalDecidePayload.description: `approval:decide`, from the person's own socket: the card's click.

ApprovalRefusalReason.description:
Why an approval was refused:

- `unknown`: no such pending approval: never stored, already declined or redeemed, or expired and gone.
- `forbidden`: another user's approval, or another conversation's.
- `expired`.
- `decided`: already decided.
- `used`: already redeemed.
- `invalid`: not a token this environment signed, or malformed.
- `mismatch`: signed, but not for the stored call.
- `channel`: a decision from a channel that may not make it.

ApprovalDecideResult.description: The answer to a decision. An approval's token goes only to the decider: the socket that clicked, or the engine that asked.

token.description: The single-use token the continuation turn redeems.

argsHash.description: What the browser checks a UI action's params against before it runs it.

ApprovalTokenClaims.description: The token's claims: a compact JWS (HS256), signed with the environment's approval key.

aid.description: The approval id, which is the tool call id.

ApprovedCall.description: What redeeming a token returns: the stored call, exactly, for the worker to run.

ApprovalStatus.description: An approval's state, for the turn that follows a decision.

ApprovalContinuation.description: What a turn that follows a decision carries, outside the message text: the token to redeem, or that the person declined.

ActionRequestApproval.description: What a UI action request carries when it runs an approved call (`OUIActionApproval`): the browser runs a `transaction` or destructive action only when this matches a grant this tab received from its own card click (ADR-0228 §2.2.6).

argsHash.description: `argsHash(params)` of the request the user approved.

ApprovalGrant.description: What the person's approval click gives this tab's OUI runtime (`runtime.grantApproval`, `OUIApprovalGrant`): the request it approved, until it expires.

expiresAt.description: Epoch ms after which the grant no longer admits anything.
